69% Upside for Affirm? Citi Thinks So, and Here's How ©@Przemek Klos from Przemek Klos via Canva, @tanaonte via Canva
Key Takeaways

Affirm is down 23% from its July high after a quarter of fast growth and higher late payments. Citi kept its Buy rating and its $115 target, 69% above today's price.

Citi's case rests on three things: volume growth above guidance, new partners that bring in more merchants, and funding costs Affirm can absorb. The September quarter supported most of it.

Citi's $115 target is 27x the earnings analysts expect over the next twelve months. That's close to the 28x Affirm has averaged since its forward P/E turned positive in 2024.

The call looks right as long as delinquencies settle after the holidays. Affirm reports that quarter in early February.

Affirm Holdings (AFRM:NASDAQ) just grew its volume 34%, and the stock is still down 23% from its July high. Citi's Bryan Keane reiterated his Buy rating and $115 price target on Nov. 11, 69% above today's price.

A strong quarter with a credit wrinkle

Affirm's fiscal first-quarter results, out Nov. 5, beat its own guidance: gross merchandise volume (GMV) rose 34% to $14.4 billion, and revenue rose 35% to $1.26 billion.

But 30-day-plus delinquencies on its monthly loans rose 35 basis points from the June quarter to 2.9%. CFO Rob O'Hare said on the call that Affirm chose to "run some experiments within the approvals and the origination" in September. Affirm also guided its December-quarter GAAP operating margin below what analysts expected, on higher warrant expense for a large partner signing up new users.

TIKR tracks 36 analysts on Affirm. How many say "Buy"?

See the full breakdown of Buy, Hold, and Sell ratings on Affirm, along with Wall Street's revenue and earnings estimates, all in one place. More than 500,000 investors use TIKR to research stocks like this one. See Affirm's Analyst Ratings

How Citi gets to $115

Keane laid out his case in an early-October note, and Affirm delivered on most of it.

He expected GMV growth at the high end of management's 27% to 30% outlook. Affirm grew 34%, and O'Hare said the business is "growing at a high 30s rate today."

He also pointed to early-stage partnerships with Intuit's QuickBooks, ServiceTitan and Amazon in the UK. CEO Max Levchin said on the call that services, the category those software partners feed, was the best performer of the categories Affirm breaks out.

And he put the hit from recent rate moves at 15 to 20 basis points of revenue less transaction costs (RLTC). Funding costs rose 27 basis points from the June quarter, yet RLTC came in at 4.3% of GMV, above management's 3.75% to 4% medium-term range.

Citi Cut Its Lucid Target for the Third Time. It Still Sees 138% Upside ©@Kittipong Jirasukhanont from PhonlamaiPhoto's Images via Canva, @Kittipong Jirasukhanont from PhonlamaiPhoto's Images via Canva
Key Takeaways

Lucid Group stock is down 78% over the past year, and on Nov. 11 Citi cut its price target to $9 from $11 and kept its Buy rating.

Citi's $9 is 138% above today's price and 37% above the $7 consensus target, which has fallen from about $24 a year ago.

The target asks for just 1.5x forward sales, but about $4.9 billion of debt and loans and $3.07 billion of preferred stock rank ahead of common shareholders.

Lucid is unlikely to reach $9 in the next year, and full-year results in late February, with 2027 guidance, are the next test.

Lucid Group (LCID:NASDAQ) has lost 78% of its value over the past year, and analysts spent this week cutting their targets after its third-quarter report. Citi's new $9 target still sits 138% above today's price of $3.78.

Fewer cars, more borrowing

Lucid delivered 3,806 vehicles in the third quarter, down 7% from a year earlier, as the US electric-vehicle market shrank 41% after federal EV tax credits ended. Free cash flow improved 30% from the second quarter but was still -$1.04 billion. So Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF), Lucid's largest investor, added $1.75 billion to its loan, which Lucid says funds it into the fourth quarter of 2027.

Citi still says Buy

Citi analyst Michael Ward kept his Buy rating on Nov. 11 and cut his target to $9 from $11, pointing to the improved cash burn. It's his third cut since he initiated coverage at $17 in March. The biggest launch he was counting on, Midsize, Lucid's lower-priced platform, has since slipped from a late-2026 start to production in the second half of 2027.

The sales math is the easy part

The average target from the 11 analysts covering Lucid has fallen from about $24 a year ago to $7, which is still 74% above the price. This chart tracks the consensus target over the past year.

Lucid Group (LCID): analysts' consensus (mean) price target, $ per share, last year (TIKR)

Those targets depend on a steep climb in sales. Analysts expect revenue to more than double in 2027, to $3.32 billion, and to double again in 2028, to $6.71 billion.

Lucid Group (LCID): revenue, actual and consensus estimates, $ billions, fiscal 2024-2028 (TIKR)

That's a lot to ask of a car that isn't due to start production until the second half of 2027. But if analysts are right, $9 is just 1.5x the sales they expect per share over the next twelve months. Lucid trades at 0.6x, near its five-year low, against a five-year average of 10x.

title: COLB's $1.2B Buyback Plan Highlights Strong Capital Returns After Q3
detail:
COLB's $1.2B Buyback Plan Highlights Strong Capital Returns After Q3

Columbia Banking System, Inc. COLB is reinforcing its shareholder-return strategy following a solid third-quarter 2026 performance. In October, the company's board of directors authorized a share repurchase program of up to $1.2 billion, reflecting management's confidence in its long-term strategy and ability to generate excess capital.

The announcement follows the completion of Columbia Banking's previous repurchase authorization. Between November 2025 and Sept. 30, 2026, the company repurchased 23.3 million common shares at an average price of $29.88, representing 7.8% of its outstanding shares as of Sept. 30, 2025. Including dividends, Columbia Banking returned more than $1 billion to shareholders over the past year.

COLB also pays out regular dividends. In November 2025, Columbia Banking increased its quarterly dividend 2.8% to 37 cents per share, signaling confidence in capital generation even with integration work still underway. In the past five years, COLB has increased its dividends twice. It has a five-year annualized dividend growth rate of 5.27% and a dividend yield of 4.8%.

Columbia Banking System, Inc. Dividend Yield (TTM)
Columbia Banking System, Inc. Dividend Yield (TTM)

Columbia Banking System, Inc. dividend-yield-ttm | Columbia Banking System, Inc. Quote

The company's capital position also remains supportive. As of Sept. 30, 2026, its common equity Tier 1 (CET1) capital ratio was 11.5%, while its total risk-based capital ratio stood at 13.8%. Both ratios remained above regulatory well-capitalized minimums and the company's long-term targets. Meanwhile, deposits increased to $52.7 billion from $52.1 billion in the preceding quarter, supporting funding stability.

Overall, the new $1.2-billion authorization underscores COLB's commitment to disciplined capital allocation and shareholder returns. However, its ability to sustain buybacks will depend on earnings generation, capital adequacy and evolving market conditions.

Other Banks Capital Distribution Activities

Citigroup C repurchased approximately $3 billion in shares in the third quarter of 2026. As of Sept. 30, 2026, $23 billion worth of shares remained available under the share repurchase program. In the third quarter 2026, Citigroup returned $4.1 billion to shareholders, including dividends, reflecting its continued focus on capital distributions alongside investments in business growth and improving profitability.

Bank of America BAC repurchased $6 billion worth of shares in third-quarter 2026, reflecting its commitment to shareholder returns. As of Sept. 30, 2026, almost $11 billion remained under its $40-billion share repurchase authorization. Including $2.2 billion in dividends, Bank of America returned $8.3 billion to shareholders in the third quarter 2026. The buybacks highlight management's confidence in its capital position, supported by a solid CET1 ratio of 10.9%.

title: Citigroup CEO offers bold S&P 500 prediction
detail:
Citigroup CEO offers bold S&P 500 prediction
Todd Campbell
Tue, November 10, 2026 at 8:33 PM MST 5 min read
C
GOOGM
Trade C on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Citigroup CEO Jane Fraser thinks recent S&P 500 weakness isn't a harbinger of a dot-com-style reckoning. Instead, Fraser said at a conference last week that the correction caused by a sell-off in technology will be shallow and over sooner rather than later.

When asked by Sara Eisen on CNBC whether the selling suggests something "deeper or longer," Fraser bluntly replied, "I don't think so."

Given that Citigroup is the 12th-largest bank on the planet with over $2.6 trillion in assets and over 217,000 employees, it has its pulse on the economy and markets, making Fraser's comments worth considering.

Fraser says S&P 500 drop not surprising, given 'priced to perfection'

The stock market is in the fourth year of a bull market, largely due to surging spending on everything and anything AI. Goldman Sachs expects hyperscalers like Google to spend $1.2 trillion on AI next year, and, according to a Bank of America note shared with me, AI activity accounted for about 1% of GDP growth through the first nine months of this year.

Fraser believes that corrections can be healthy, a long-held Wall Street belief, because removing frothiness means money on the sidelines that can later be redeployed. She appears unshocked by the Nasdaq's 10% retreat from its summertime highs, or last week's 5.5% drop on November 5.

"I don't think any of us should be particularly surprised," said Fraser. "We are two, three days after the election with a major shift in the results there. And we all know there is a confluence of factors here between the war and some of the AI concerns."

Fraser pointed out that the market was "priced to perfection," but noted that selling was largely due to hedge funds rethinking their risk exposure, rather than to mutual funds or retail investors.

"If you take a step back, what are we seeing underneath all of this? It's really action taken by the hedge funds to de-risk. We're seeing them buying back short positions, and we're seeing them sell long positions."

Citigroup CEO Jane Fraser thinks the stock drop won't be deep because AI demand is 'real.'Bloomberg / Getty Images
Why Citigroup CEO thinks a drop would be shallow

Concerns largely stem from the worry that companies are spending too much on AI capacity and increasingly borrowing to finance it. The bear argument is that if IT budgets tap the brakes on AI use due to costs, it could leave the industry with too little demand to repay debt and lead to write-downs on unused infrastructure.

Hedge funds tend to react more quickly to potential risks and rewards than other asset managers and retail investors because they often run leveraged, exposing them to greater gains and losses.

title: Goldman, Citi and Other Banks Reportedly Fund $270 Million Stablecoin Initiative
detail:
Goldman, Citi and Other Banks Reportedly Fund $270 Million Stablecoin Initiative
Goldman, Citi and other banks reportedly commit $270 million to Project Faro
Unchained
Tue, November 10, 2026 at 1:20 PM MST 2 min read
GS
C
SAN
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

The stablecoin venture that 21 financial firms unveiled in September has about $270 million in commitments from its backers, with Goldman Sachs, Citigroup, Banco Santander and Deutsche Bank among the banks putting up money, according to a report on Tuesday that cited people familiar with the matter.

The funding is meant to pay for the planned issuer's first five years, the report said. Its backers plan to incorporate the issuer, codenamed Project Faro, in the U.S. and are still looking for a chief executive, according to the report.

Versions of the report published by other outlets did not say whether the money is equity or another form of capital, how much each bank is putting in, or which blockchain the token will use. No bank or the venture has commented publicly on the report.

Get Unchained's crypto news in your inbox with the free Unchained Daily newsletter.

Two Issuers Hold Most of the Supply

The group's first token will be pegged to the U.S. dollar, a market where two issuers account for most of the supply. Tether's USDT and Circle's USDC made up about 84% of the roughly $293 billion in dollar-pegged stablecoins in circulation on Tuesday, Unchained calculated from DefiLlama's stablecoin data. USDT had about $176 billion outstanding and USDC about $70 billion.

What the Group Announced in September

The 21 firms said on Sept. 1 that they would set up a new company in the second half of 2026, subject to closing conditions, to issue a stablecoin, and Unchained reported on the plan that day. A dollar token comes first, with a longer-term aim of expanding to other Group of Seven (G7) currencies, a euro version being the priority. The group is targeting the first half of 2027 to go to market.

Besides the four lenders the report named as committing the money, members include Bank of America, Wells Fargo, Fidelity Investments, BBVA, Lloyds Banking Group and MUFG Bank. The effort grew out of a group of 10 banks that said in October 2025 it was exploring a reserve-backed form of digital money.

The group said it intends to comply with the U.S. Guiding and Establishing National Innovation for U.S. Stablecoins (GENIUS) Act and the European Union's Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA) regulation, "as applicable." The Sept. 1 announcement said the company's name would be announced later.

The group also faces other bank and corporate token efforts, some involving the same banks. JPMorgan, Citi, Bank of America and Wells Fargo plan a tokenized deposit network, which would put customer bank deposits on a blockchain, for 2027, while the Open USD stablecoin, whose backers include Coinbase, Visa and Stripe, already has about $924 million in circulation, according to DefiLlama.
